supported_scope: Execution of agent shell commands within OS-level sandbox boundaries using native OS features (nsjail on Linux, sandbox-exec on macOS, AppContainer on Windows) with configurable containment and permission rules.
unsupported_scope: Running commands without sandbox restrictions by default (sandbox is disabled by default).
Commands that require network access outside approved domains unless explicitly allowed.
Commands that require access to sensitive files like ~/.ssh and .env which are blocked by default.
unestablished_scope: Whether all possible agent actions beyond shell commands are sandboxed.
Exact enforcement details for non-filesystem or non-network resources.
Sandbox behavior on platforms other than Linux, macOS, and Windows.
required_setup: Enable the terminal sandbox by setting "enableTerminalSandbox" to true in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json and configure "toolPermission" to control sandbox execution behavior (e.g., "proceed-in-sandbox").
constraints: Sandbox is disabled by default ("enableTerminalSandbox" default is false).
User must approve commands that request to run outside the sandbox unless matching an unsandboxed allow rule.
Filesystem access is limited to mounted paths per permissions; denied paths are blocked.
Network access is blocked by default except for domains allowed under read_url permissions.
Escape hatch commands require explicit allow rules or user approval.
Interactive prompts appear for commands needing review or sandbox bypass approval.

evidence.quote: The terminal sandbox is a lightweight security isolation mechanism that protects your host system from potentially destructive file manipulations or unauthorized outbound network requests when the agent executes local shell commands.
evidence.claim: Describes the sandbox as a security isolation mechanism for agent shell commands.

evidence.section: Terminal sandbox > Antigravity CLI > CLI permissions integration
evidence.quote: Filesystem : Workspace folders and paths allowed under write_file are mounted read-write. Paths allowed under read_file are mounted read-only, on top of the default system mounts. Denied paths are blocked, and everything else is inaccessible.
evidence.claim: Sandbox enforces filesystem boundaries based on permissions.

evidence.section: Terminal sandbox > Antigravity CLI > How it works
evidence.quote: With the terminal sandbox enabled, Antigravity CLI executes commands inside an OS-level isolation boundary. Commands can write to your workspace, temporary directories, and common build caches, and read system directories such as /usr and /etc so your tools keep working.
evidence.claim: Sandbox runs commands inside OS-level isolation boundaries with controlled filesystem access.

evidence.section: Terminal sandbox > Antigravity CLI > Interactive prompts
evidence.quote: When the agent asks to bypass the sandbox, the prompt calls it out explicitly so you can judge the risk: Approving “always allow” here records an unsandboxed(...) rule instead of a plain command(...) rule.
evidence.claim: User approval is required to bypass sandbox restrictions, with explicit prompts.
